title: Cash on Delivery in Pakistan — The Only Payment Method That Lets You Inspect Before You Pay
author: Omar Farooq
authorBio: Founder of BazaarNow. Has been shipping products across Pakistan since 2024. Believes COD is the greatest invention since the wicketkeeper decided to stand back.
excerpt: COD isn't just a payment method — it's the reason online shopping works in Pakistan. Here's how to use it without getting burned, why we offer it despite the risk, and the one situation where you should pay in advance instead.

sections.content: Cash on delivery handles 85% of all e-commerce transactions in Pakistan (State Bank of Pakistan, 2024). Read that again. Eight-five percent. That's not a preference — it's a verdict. Pakistanis don't trust online stores until they've held the product in their hands. And honestly, they shouldn't.

sections.title: The Short Version
items: COD lets you inspect the product before paying a single rupee
It's available on every single order at BazaarNow — no minimum, no extra fee
If the package looks tampered with, don't accept it. Simple as that
Advance payment (JazzCash, EasyPaisa, bank transfer) gets you 5% off — and yes, we'll explain when that's worth it

sections.text: COD is not a feature. It's trust infrastructure

sections.content: Here's a thing most e-commerce founders won't say out loud: COD is expensive for the seller. Returns are higher. Cash handling is messy. The rider has to collect money from someone who might have gone to get doodh from the corner shop exactly when the delivery arrives. (This happens roughly 47% of the time. I did not do a formal study. I count my frustrations.)

So why do we offer it? Because Pakistani shoppers have been burned. They've paid in advance and received a brick in a box. They've transferred money and watched the seller's WhatsApp DP disappear into the void. COD is the only thing standing between a customer and a very expensive disappointment. We'd rather eat the return cost than ask you to trust us blind.

sections.text: The three rules of COD that nobody tells you
1. Open the package before you hand over the cash

sections.content: The delivery rider will wait. They're supposed to. You have every right to open the package, check the product against what you ordered, and only then pay. If the rider tries to rush you — and some will, because they've got thirty more stops — politely tell them this is the only way you do COD. Nine times out of ten, they'll wait. The tenth time, call us. We'll sort it.

sections.text: 2. If the seal is broken, refuse it

sections.content: A tampered package is a red flag the size of Minar-e-Pakistan. If the tape is cut, re-taped, or looks like someone played frisbee with your box, don't accept it. Tell the rider to mark it as damaged. Contact us immediately. We'll ship a replacement the same day — no arguments, no investigation panel, no 'please send pictures of all six angles.' We trust you. That's the whole point.

sections.text: 3. Have the exact amount ready. Or at least close

sections.content: Delivery riders don't carry change for a Rs. 5,000 note at 8 PM. They've had a long day. Their chai has gone cold. If your order is Rs. 1,847, try to have something close to that. The rider will appreciate it. So will the next customer on his route who doesn't have to wait while he runs to the tuck shop for khulla.

sections.text: When you should NOT use COD

sections.content: I know I just spent 350 words telling you COD is the backbone of Pakistani e-commerce. It is. But here's the thing — we give you 5% off when you pay in advance. And there's exactly one situation where that makes more sense than COD.

You've ordered from us before. You know we deliver what we show. At that point, COD is just making the rider carry cash for no reason. Switch to JazzCash, EasyPaisa, or a bank transfer. Save 5%. On a Rs. 6,000 order, that's Rs. 300 — enough for a decent biryani with raita. Check our [special offers page](/offers) for the full breakdown. (We've done the math. Biryani economics is a core competency here.)

items: Discount applied: 5% of your order total, auto-calculated at checkout

sections.content: We don't hold inventory (we wrote that in small print on the checkout page — go look, it's there). Once you place your order, we arrange the product through our partner network and deliver it to you. If it arrives damaged or not as advertised, you get a full refund — see our [return policy](/returns) for the details. No 'store credit.' No 'we'll give you 20% off your next order.' Full refund. Back to your wallet.

You're looking for a store that ships in 2 hours. We deliver in 2-4 working days. If you need a birthday gift for a party that starts in 45 minutes — we are not your solution. Go to the physical bazaar. Buy something nice. Come back to us for the next birthday. We'll still be here, shipping in 2-4 working days, making dad jokes in the product descriptions.

sections.text: Straight answers to the questions everyone asks

items.q: Is COD really free on BazaarNow?
items.a: Yes. No extra charge. No hidden fee. No minimum order amount. The price you see is the price you pay when the rider arrives.

items.q: What if I'm not home when the delivery arrives?
items.a: The rider will call you. If you can't receive it, we'll reschedule for the next day. If that happens twice, we'll have a gentle conversation about time management. (Gentle. We promise.)

items.q: Can I return something I bought with COD?
items.a: Within 7 days, absolutely. Contact us on WhatsApp at 0310 1418307. We'll arrange a pickup. Once we receive the item, we refund you via JazzCash, EasyPaisa, or bank transfer — whichever you prefer.

items.q: Do you deliver to my city?
items.a: We deliver to 100+ cities across Pakistan. Lahore, Karachi, Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Faisalabad, Multan, Peshawar, Quetta, and many more. Check the full list at checkout.

items.q: Is my information safe when I order COD?
items.a: We only use your name, phone, and address to deliver your order. Nothing else. We don't sell data. We don't 'share with marketing partners.' We're a store, not a data brokerage pretending to be a store.

items.q: Why should I trust a store I found online?
items.a: Because you're paying after you inspect. That's the beauty of COD. If we send you a brick in a box — you don't pay. We lose the product, the shipping, and our dignity. The incentives are aligned in your favor.

sections.content: COD is the reason you can shop online in Pakistan without that knot in your stomach. Use it. It's there for you. And when you're ready to trust us enough to pay in advance — we'll buy you biryani. Metaphorically. In the form of a 5% discount. Which you should absolutely spend on actual biryani.
